holidays.name: National Aunt and Uncle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the fun aunts and uncles who spoil nieces and nephews with sweets, secrets, and questionable life advice, all without having to do the bedtime routine.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially in the United States, it grew from the popularity of social media tribute days and greeting card culture. It was promoted by family-focused observance calendars, though it has no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: The word 'avuncular' describes behavior that is kindly and uncle-like, and it comes from the Latin word 'avunculus,' meaning maternal uncle.

holidays.name: National Coffee Milkshake Day
holidays.description: A caffeinated twist on the classic milkshake, perfect for anyone who can't decide between a dessert and a morning pick-me-up. Blend coffee, ice cream, and milk, then slurp away.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance listed on American food-holiday calendars. Its exact creator is unknown, but it fits the tradition of dessert-themed days that celebrate popular diner treats.
holidays.funFact: Milkshakes originally contained whiskey in the 1880s, and were marketed as an energizing eggnog-like tonic before becoming the sweet, non-alcoholic treat we know today.

holidays.name: Bagelfest Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the chewy, boiled-then-baked ring of carbohydrate joy, with cream cheese, lox, or whatever toppings you dare to pile on.
holidays.origin: Bagelfest is a real festival held in Mattoon, Illinois, where the Lenders Bagels factory once operated. The town began hosting the event in the late 1980s, and it grew into an annual celebration with parades, contests, and a lot of bagels.
holidays.funFact: Mattoon once set a world record for the largest bagel ever made, which was a heavyweight achievement for a small Illinois town.

holidays.name: Gorgeous Grandma Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to honoring the stylish, sassy, and wonderful grandmothers in our lives. Compliment grandma on her looks, her cookies, and her unmatched storytelling.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance is tied to the feast day of St. Anne, who is traditionally considered the grandmother of Jesus and the patron saint of grandmothers. July 26 is her feast day in many Christian traditions.
holidays.funFact: St. Anne is the patron saint of grandmothers, as well as of homemakers, miners, and equestrians, which is quite a diverse portfolio.

holidays.name: Moon Day Eve of Cow Appreciation: Cow Parade Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek celebration for people who love all things bovine, from cow-print outfits to leaving a polite moo in the pasture.
holidays.origin: Cow-themed observances grew out of agricultural fairs and public art events like the CowParade, which began in Zurich in 1998 and later spread to cities around the world, featuring decorated fiberglass cows.
holidays.funFact: The CowParade became one of the largest public art events in the world, with thousands of painted cow sculptures displayed in cities like Chicago and New York.
